proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity at all, so we have added HDI's defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement claims relating to the Site, HDI's breach of law, unauthorised access to Content or customer data caused by HDI, and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure. Our reciprocal indemnity is deliberately narrow (limited to Content and Marks we provide and our own breach of law), and we have placed these provisions in Section 9 so they survive under Section 10.7; if HDI prefers, we can discuss customary IP exclusions and remedies.

ops.text: (c) Indemnification by HDI. HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (1) an allegation that the Site, or any materials, software, technology or services provided by HDI, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right (other than to the extent arising from Content or Marks provided by the Company); (2) HDI's breach of any applicable law, rule or regulation; (3) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Confidential Information, Content or customer information caused by HDI; or (4) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

(d) Indemnification by the Company. The Company shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless HDI from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (1) an allegation that the Content or Marks provided by the Company to HDI infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right, or (2) the Company's breach of any applicable law, rule or regulation.

(e) Procedure. The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of any claim for which indemnification is sought, and the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of such claim, provided that no settlement imposing any liability or obligation on, or requiring any admission by, the indemnified Party shall be made without its prior written consent. The indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate in the defense with counsel of its own choosing at its own expense.

proposal.summary: Insert mutual indemnification provisions into Section 9, with HDI covering IP infringement, breach of law, data/Content security incidents and wilful misconduct, and our indemnity limited to Content and Marks we supply.

rationale: The Agreement contains no indemnification, hold-harmless or defence language anywhere: Section 9 (Warranties) is limited to corporate authority reps and the Globix carve-out, and Section 10 is boilerplate general provisions. HDI designs, develops, hosts and operates the Site and supplies the software, technology and hosting environment, and it also handles our Confidential Information, Content and customer information, yet bears no obligation to defend us against third-party IP infringement claims or claims arising from its own breach of law, security failures or wilful misconduct. That is the playbook walk-away position (no Vendor IP indemnity). We therefore insert an HDI defence and indemnity for third-party IP claims relating to the Site and HDI-supplied materials, HDI's breach of law, unauthorised access to Content/customer data caused by HDI, and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct, plus a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, with our reciprocal indemnity kept narrow to the Content and Marks we supply and our own breach of law. Placement within Section 9 avoids renumbering and captures the existing Section 10.7 survival of Section 9.

HDI keeps its pre-existing platform and tools and gives us a perpetual, royalty-free licence to anything of its embedded in the Site; if HDI prefers, we can instead leave ownership of the underlying build with HDI provided we receive that perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site deliverables.

ops.text: 5.5 Ownership. As between the Parties, the Company owns and retains all right, title and interest in and to (i) the Content, the Marks and all other materials furnished by the Company, (ii) the Site, including its design, look and feel, and all work product, deliverables and materials developed by or for HDI specifically for the Site, and (iii) all customer, order and e-mail list data generated through the Site in respect of Deerskin Products, and HDI hereby assigns to the Company all right, title and interest it may have in the items described in clauses (ii) and (iii). HDI retains all right, title and interest in its pre-existing software, tools, systems and hosting platform, and hereby grants the Company a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense any such HDI materials to the extent incorporated in, or necessary for the operation of, the Site. Nothing in this Agreement assigns to HDI, or creates any joint ownership in, any intellectual property, Content or data of the Company.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 5.5 vesting ownership of the Site deliverables, Content and Site customer data in the Company, with HDI retaining its pre-existing platform and granting a licence-back, and no joint ownership.

quote: The Company shall have exclusive artistic and editorial control over the Site, including, without limitation, the implementation of the Content on the Site and the design and look and feel of the Site.
rationale: The Agreement contains no intellectual property or data ownership provision at all: HDI designs, develops and hosts the Site and holds the Company's Content, user information and data (p0048), yet nothing states who owns the Site deliverables, the Content or the customer/order data generated through the Site. Section 5.2 gives us only artistic and editorial control, Section 10.2 disclaims co-ownership only as to the relationship, and the confidentiality section protects but does not vest ownership. Under the IP rule we must own the deliverables and materials created for us, retain all rights in our Content, Marks and customer data, and avoid any implied assignment to or joint ownership with the Vendor, while HDI keeps its pre-existing platform subject to a licence-back. Proposed new Section 5.5 inserted after 5.4 supplies the preferred position with a minimal, self-contained clause; the fallback (HDI ownership of the build plus a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free licence to us) is offered in the comment.

ops.text: (c) Limitation of Liability. Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the fees paid or payable by the Company to HDI under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (ii) One Million Dollars ($1,000,000), and neither Party shall be liable to the other for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential or punitive damages. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. The Company's obligations to make payments pursuant to Sections 3 and 4.2 shall not be deemed damages subject to this Section 9(c).

proposal.summary: Add a mutual liability cap (greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000) with consequential damages exclusion and uncapped Excluded Claims

rationale: The Agreement has no limitation-of-liability provision: a full read of the document (development/hosting obligations, fees, term, exclusivity, confidentiality, warranties and general provisions) returns no "aggregate liability", damages exclusion or cap language, and searches for "liability", "damages" and "indemnif" surface only the no-joint-venture clause. Both parties are therefore exposed to unlimited direct and consequential liability, including HDI as hosting provider handling the Company's Content, customer data and Confidential Information. Because the Company pays HDI 30% of Net Sales under Section 3, a fee-based cap is a meaningful base. We insert a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, a mutual exclusion of indirect damages, and uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement), with the Company's payment obligations excluded from the cap. Placement as Section 9(c) keeps the provision within a section that survives termination under Section 10.7.

quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
rationale:
Section 4.2 imposes a stipulated sum payable by the Company (our client, the customer) to HDI, so the rule is engaged in the flagged direction. The planner hint of "likelyAbsent" was incorrect: although the document uses no "liquidated damages" label, the Termination Payment is functionally a Customer-payable liquidated amount.

It breaches the preferred position (no LD or penalty payable by Customer) and reaches the walk-away threshold on quantum. Fees under Section 3.1 are 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month, whereas the Termination Payment is 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 — a bill that exceeds a full year of actual fees (e.g. at $2m Net Sales: fees ~$560k/yr versus a ~$600k termination payment), and so exceeds remaining contract value. It is also triggered by any Company termination, including ordinary non-renewal on 90 days' notice under Section 4.1 and termination for HDI's own breach (only the narrow Section 1.6 late-launch right is expressly "without penalty"). The arrangement is one-way: Section 4.1 lets HDI walk on the same 90 days' notice for nothing, and p0028 confirms HDI never pays the Company.

I proposed the fallback rather than outright deletion because Section 1.2 has HDI bearing all Site design, development, hosting and promotion costs, recouping only through the revenue share, so some early-termination compensation is part of the genuine bargain and pure deletion would be disproportionate. The redline therefore caps the payment at three months' Section 3.1 fees, makes it the sole monetary remedy, and disapplies it where we terminate for HDI's breach or under Section 1.6.

quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
rationale: There is no minimum purchase commitment or volume cap on us: Section 3.1 charges HDI's 30% share only on actual Net Sales above $11,000 per month, and Section 6.1 is an exclusivity (not volume) restriction. However, Section 4.2(a) attaches a penalty to our only exit route: the one-year term auto-renews annually (Section 4.1) and if the Company gives the 90-day termination notice it must pay HDI half of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000, in eight quarterly installments, for services it will never receive. That is a take-or-pay style charge on exit rather than a true-up, contrary to our position that fees are payable for usage or services actually delivered. Because HDI bears all design, hosting and promotion costs (Sections 1.2, 1.6, 1.8), outright deletion is disproportionate, so we take the fallback: cap the payment at HDI's documented unrecovered Site costs (a true-up) and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's breach or failure to launch under Section 1.6.

quote: This Agreement shall not be deemed to create a partnership or joint venture and neither Party is the other's agent, partner, employee or representative.
rationale: Searches for "solicit", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel" and "employ" return no personnel covenant; the only "shall not" restrictions are the exclusivity provisions (p0037, p0042), confidentiality (p0048, p0053, p0054) and the no-joint-venture clause (p0061), and the only references to employees are incidental (indemnity and relationship-of-parties language). Section 5.4's appointed-representative provisions likewise impose no hiring restraint. Since no non-solicitation or no-hire obligation binds the Company (our client), the agreement already meets our preferred position of no non-solicit on the Customer, and no redline is needed.

proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice from 90 to 30 days and require HDI renewal reminder 60 days before each anniversary.

quote: This Agreement shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other.
rationale: Section 4.1 auto-renews for successive one-year terms (acceptable term length), but the non-renewal notice window is 90 days, which exceeds both our preferred 30-day window and the 60-day fallback, and there is no vendor reminder before renewal. Fees are a fixed revenue share (Section 3.1) with no escalation mechanism, so no uplift cap is required. Redline shortens the notice to 30 days and adds a 60-day HDI renewal reminder; a 60-day window is our fallback.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a wind-down provision because the Agreement is silent on exit: HDI hosts the Site and holds our Content, customer and order data, but has no obligation to help us migrate or to return that data on termination. Consistent with our playbook, this gives us up to six (6) months of transition assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return of our data in a machine-readable format within thirty (30) days, and deletion with written certification thereafter; we can discuss a ninety (90) day assistance period if the six-month tail is a concern.

ops.text: 4.3 Transition Assistance; Return of Company Data. Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, HDI shall (a) at the Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance, including reasonable cooperation in migrating the Site and the Company's data to the Company or its designee, for a period of up to six (6) months following the Termination Date at HDI's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days following the Termination Date, return to the Company all Content, user information, customer and order data and other data of the Company in HDI's possession or control, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete all such Content and data from its systems and certify such deletion to the Company in writing. This Section 4.3 shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Insert new Section 4.3 requiring HDI to provide up to six months of transition assistance and to return, then delete and certify deletion of, Company Content and customer/order data.

quote: unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other. Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated (the "Termination Date").
rationale: Section 4 addresses only term, notice and the Termination Payment (p0024-p0029), and no other provision addresses exit. HDI hosts the Site on its own server (p0007) and holds our Content, user information and data (p0009, p0016, p0048), yet there is no obligation to provide transition or migration assistance, to return that Content and customer/order data on termination, or to delete it and certify deletion. Section 10.7 survival (p0068) covers Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 only and does not cure the gap. This is the playbook's missing-transition scenario in a hosting agreement, so we insert a new Section 4.3 in the termination section reflecting the preferred position (six months' assistance at HDI's then-current rates, return within thirty days in machine-readable format, deletion plus written certification), with the 90-day fallback available.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 9 contains only mutual corporate authority representations, so HDI gives no warranty at all for the Site it develops, hosts and maintains. We have added our standard performance warranty (professional and workmanlike services, Site conformance to specifications for twelve (12) months, compliance with law, no malicious code) with a re-performance/repair/refund remedy; we can accept a ninety (90) day conformance period as a fallback.

ops.text: (c) HDI represents and warrants that (1) all services performed by HDI under this Agreement, including the design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance, management and hosting of the Site, will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (2) for a period of twelve (12) months following the Company's written acceptance of the Site (or of any modification or enhancement thereto) pursuant to Section 5.2, the Site will conform in all material respects to the specifications and documentation agreed by the Parties; (3) HDI's performance under this Agreement will comply with all applicable laws, rules and regulations; and (4) the Site, and any software or code delivered or used by HDI in connection with the Site, will not contain any virus, worm, time bomb, disabling device or other malicious code. The Company's remedy for breach of the foregoing warranties shall be, at HDI's option, re-performance of the non-conforming services or repair or replacement of the non-conforming portion of the Site and, if HDI fails to cure within thirty (30) days of notice, a refund of the fees paid by the Company with respect to the non-conforming services. The foregoing express warranties shall not be limited or superseded by any disclaimer of warranties elsewhere in this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Add an HDI performance warranty (workmanlike services, Site conformance for 12 months, legal compliance, no malicious code) with a re-perform/repair/refund remedy in Section 9.

rationale: Section 9 ("Warranties") contains only mutual corporate existence/authority representations (p0056-p0057) and a Globix-specific acknowledgement (p0058). Nothing in Sections 1, 5 or 9 obliges HDI to perform the design, development, hosting and maintenance services in a workmanlike manner, to have the Site conform to agreed specifications for any period, to comply with applicable law, or to keep the Site free of malicious code, and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy exists. There is also no warranty disclaimer, so inserting an express warranty is a clean addition. Per the playbook this absence is a deviation requiring insertion, so we added a new Section 9(c) with a 12-month Site conformance period and a re-perform/repair/refund remedy, flagging the 90-day fallback.

If the cyber limit is an issue, we can accept E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber liability of USD 2,000,000.

ops.text: 10.9 Insurance. HDI shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: (a) commercial general liability insurance of not less than $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 in the aggregate; (b) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than $2,000,000; (c) cyber liability insurance of not less than $5,000,000 covering HDI's processing of Confidential Information, Content and customer or user data; and (d) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. HDI shall provide the Company with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.summary: Insert insurance covenant (CGL, E&O, cyber, workers' comp) as new Section 10.9

quote: 10.8 Headings; Counterparts. The section headings in this Agreement are for reference purposes only and shall not define, limit or affect the meaning or interpretation of this Agreement.
rationale: No insurance provision appears anywhere in the Agreement (searches for "insurance" and "indemn" return nothing, and Section 10 General Provisions ends at 10.8 Headings; Counterparts). HDI is a hosting/services vendor: it stores and operates the Site on its systems (1.4), processes customer orders and export files (1.5, 2.2), and has access to Content, user information and data (8.1). Under the playbook this warrants standard vendor coverage, so we insert a new Section 10.9 requiring CGL of USD 1M/2M, E&O of USD 2M, cyber liability of USD 5M and statutory workers' compensation, with certificates on request. Placed in the general provisions section, which also survives termination for two years under 10.7. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M offered in the comment.
